title: Three Days and One Short Song
subtitle: 节日庆典 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 节日庆典（人与社会·历史社会与文化）
meta: 主题语境：节日庆典（人与社会·历史社会与文化）　|　核心词汇：festival　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 festival 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 my grandmother ① held a festival that no neighbour in the valley would have forgotten, and she said the holding was the whole of the autumn. The ② festival, meaning the celebration itself and not the day, ran three days and stayed unwritten in the book; a festival, she said, is the only thing in a valley that is judged by how long it is left unwritten.

Every ③ festival in that valley had the same short song beside it, and the ④ festival at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the harvest and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A festival, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to remember; my grandmother said the remembering is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the festival was the whole of the matter, meaning the rejoicing and not the celebration. The ⑥ festival, meaning the rejoicing and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody writes down; festival, he said, is either something you hold or the only word that means both a celebration and a rejoicing. He said the rejoicing is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ festival had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short song. The ⑧ festival of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in October, was one valley and three days of remembering; festival, she said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to remember. She said the remembering was never mentioned.

The ⑨ festival I remember is the one written in the plan, which closed in 1970 and is still described as the quietest in the valley. A ⑩ festival, my mother said in 1972, is the only one that improves by being remembered; every festival, she said, is a rejoicing that has agreed to look like a celebration. She said the rejoicing was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 节日；庆典（指山谷里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 节日（指那一个本身，与日子相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold a festival 举办一场节日庆典
D. n. 节日（指留给收成的那一个）
E. n. 节日（抽象总称，指一个山谷的庆典之事）
F. n. 节日（指计划里写到、被人记住的那一个）
G. n. 欢庆；热闹（指一件事里人人都等却无人写下的那样东西）
H. n. 欢庆（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人写下的那样东西）

items.q: held a festival that no neighbour in the valley would have forgotten
The festival, meaning the celebration itself and not the day
the festival at the far end
the festival was the whole of the matter
the festival had become a line in a plan
The festival of the whole thing
A festival, my mother said in 1972

answers.why: hold a festival 意为“举办一场节日庆典”，1961 年祖母办了一场山谷里没有一位邻居肯忘记的庆典。
festival 意为“节日”，指那一个本身而不是日子，它持续了三天而在簿子上没有被写下。
festival 意为“节日”，指山谷里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一支短短的歌。
festival 意为“节日”，指留给收成的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
festival 意为“欢庆、热闹”，指一件事里人人都等却无人写下的那样东西，叔叔说这场欢庆就是那件事的全部。
festival 意为“欢庆”，指人人都等却无人写下的那样东西而不是那一场庆典，是事情里人人都等、却无人写下的东西。
festival 意为“节日”，指计划里写到、被人记住的那一个，到 1968 年这一个成了计划里的一行。
festival 意为“节日”，祖母十月写道，整件事的庆典之事是一个山谷和三天的记挂。
festival 意为“节日”，我记得的是计划里写下的那一个，1970 年结束了，至今仍被说成山谷里最安静的一个。
festival 为抽象总称，母亲 1972 年说，一个节日是唯一会因为被好好记住而变得更好的东西。
